# Arkiv Chain Indexer

> A block explorer for an Arkiv chain: blocks, transactions, wallets, fees and rent, and the entities
> stored on chain with their typed attributes. Every page is reachable by URL, and every filter or
> query lives in the URL's query string, so a link reproduces exactly what the page shows.

Paths below are relative to this site's origin. Pages are rendered in the browser (a React app); to read
data without rendering, use the JSON API under `/api/` (see the last section). Amounts are in wei, and
the native token is shown with the site's configured symbol. An entity is permanent when its expiry
block is 18446744073709551615 (2^64 − 1). Arkiv transactions pay rent for storage beside their gas fee;
rent is burned outside gas and is never counted as part of the fee.

## Pages

- [Home](/): search box, latest blocks and latest transactions.
- [Search](/search?q=0x...): `q` is a block number, transaction hash, address or entity key; lists the
  pages that match it.
- [Blocks](/blocks): stored blocks with gas, base fee, burned gas fees and rent.
  Parameters: `blockGt`, `blockLt` (block numbers, exclusive), `dateGt`, `dateLt` (ISO-8601 timestamps,
  e.g. `2026-10-30T12:00:00Z`), `limit` (10, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000 or 10000; default 1000).
  Example: `/blocks?blockGt=1000&blockLt=2000&limit=500`
- [Block](/block?block=12345): one block with its transactions. `block` is the block number.
- [Transactions](/transactions): stored transactions, newest first.
  Parameters: `block` (one exact block), `blockGt`, `blockLt`, `dateGt`, `dateLt`, `address` (sent from
  or to this address), `nonceGt`, `nonceLt` (with `address`), `limit` (rows per page, at most 1000),
  `page` (1-based). Example: `/transactions?address=0xabc...&limit=100&page=2`
- [Transaction](/tx/0x...): `/tx/<transaction hash>`. Gas fee, rent and total cost, and each Arkiv
  operation in the transaction (create, patch, extend, transfer, delete) with its entity,
  expiry and attributes.
- [Wallets](/senders): the most active sender addresses. Parameter: `limit` (default 100).
- [Address](/address/0x...): `/address/<address>`. A wallet's current balance and its transactions; takes
  the same filters as Transactions except `address`.
- [Entity](/entity/0x...): `/entity/<entity key>`. An entity's indexed history: current state (live,
  expired or deleted), owner, expiry, attributes, and one row per operation with its rent.
- [Entity explorer](/entity-explorer): queries the chain's node for the entities stored right now (see the
  next section).
- [Statistics](/statistics): chain-wide totals: transactions, operations, gas fees, rent, entity counts,
  attribute types and the most used schemas.
- [Ranges](/ranges): per-range aggregates of block metrics.
  Parameters: `rangeSize` (2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500 or 1000 blocks; default 100),
  `rangeStartGt`, `rangeStartLt`, `dateGt`, `dateLt`, `limit`.
- [Charts](/charts): historical charts of block metrics.
  Parameters: `blockStart`, `blockEnd`, `startDate` (ISO-8601), `xAxisMode` (`blocks` or `dates`),
  `zoom` (index into the bucket sizes 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 150, 300, 1000 blocks), `points`, and
  `parameters` (comma-separated series names, default `averageBaseFeeWei,averagePriorityFeeWei`).
- [Records](/records): the transactions with the most gas used, the highest fee and the highest
  effective gas price.
- [Activity](/activity): the senders using the most gas recently. Parameters: `window` (`1h`, `6h` or
  `24h`), `address` (one sender's per-minute history).

## Entity explorer and its query language

The entity explorer runs a query against the chain's node and lists the matching entities: key,
schema, owner, attributes and expiry. Its whole state is in the URL:

- `q`: the query (required to show results). URL-encode it (`encodeURIComponent`): spaces as `%20` or
  `+`, `=` as `%3D`, `&` as `%26`.
- `pageSize`: entities per page: 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 (default 50).
- `expiration`: `all` (default) or `soon` (only entities expiring within 24 hours).

`q` may also be a bare entity key (`0x` + 64 hex characters), read as `$key = key(0x...)`, or a bare
address (`0x` + 40 hex characters), read as `$owner = addr(0x...)`.

Query syntax:

- A condition compares an attribute with a typed literal: `name = str('open')`. Operators: `=`, `!=`,
  `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.
- Literals are written as type constructors: `str('text')`, `i32(-5)`, `u64(1200000)`, `u256(10)`,
  `dec(3.5)`, `addr(0x...)`, `key(0x...)`, `bytes32(0x...)`, and bare `true` / `false`. Inside `str('...')`
  a single quote is doubled: `str('it''s')`.
- `name STARTSWITH str('prefix')` is a prefix match on a str attribute.
- `EXISTS(name)` is true when the attribute is set with any type; `TYPEOF(name) = u64` when it is set with
  exactly that type (`bool`, `i32`, `u64`, `u256`, `dec`, `bytes32`, `str`, `addr`, `key`).
- Combine with `AND`, `OR` and `NOT` (case-insensitive; `&&` and `||` are not accepted) and parentheses.
  `--` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
- Entity fields: `$key`, `$owner`, `$creator` (addresses), `$createdAt`, `$expiresAt` (block numbers,
  compare with `u64(...)`).
- Attribute names start with a letter and may contain letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`; type names and
  keywords cannot be used as names. Entities written through a named schema carry the indexed str
  attribute `arkiv.schema`.
- Only indexed attributes are ever matched. Attributes stored without the indexed flag, and every
  `bytes` attribute, are returned in results but never match a condition.

Examples (query, then the URL that runs it):

- All entities of one schema:
  `arkiv.schema = str('note')`
  `/entity-explorer?q=arkiv.schema%20%3D%20str('note')`
- One owner's entities created after block 100000, 10 per page:
  `$owner = addr(0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111) AND $createdAt > u64(100000)`
  `/entity-explorer?q=%24owner%20%3D%20addr(0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111)%20AND%20%24createdAt%20%3E%20u64(100000)&pageSize=10`
- Open tickets or anything without a `closedAt` attribute:
  `status = str('open') OR NOT EXISTS(closedAt)`
  `/entity-explorer?q=status%20%3D%20str('open')%20OR%20NOT%20EXISTS(closedAt)`
- One entity by key: `/entity-explorer?q=0x<64 hex characters>`

The explorer reads the node, so it shows entities as they are now. For an entity's past versions and
operations, open `/entity/<entity key>`.

## JSON API

The pages read a public JSON API at `/api/...`. List endpoints return compact rows: one `names` array
plus an array of values per row. The full reference, with every parameter and response field, is in the
repository README: https://github.com/Arkiv-Network/arkiv-chain-indexer#http-server

- `/api/blocks`: blocks; same filters as the Blocks page (`blockGt`, `blockLt`, `dateGt`, `dateLt`, `limit`).
- `/api/block/<number>`: one block with its transactions.
- `/api/transactions`: transactions; same filters as the Transactions page.
- `/api/transaction/<hash>`: one transaction with its decoded Arkiv operations.
- `/api/entity/<entity key>`: an entity's operations and current indexed state.
- `/api/search?q=<text>`: what a block number, hash, address or entity key refers to.
- `/api/ranges?rangeSize=<n>`: range aggregates.
- `/api/senders`: wallet activity.
- `/api/statistics`: chain-wide statistics.
- `/api/sync`: how far the indexer is behind the chain head.
- `/api/balances/live?address=<address>`: an address's current balance, read from the node.
